question: A potential receiver:

options.opa: It is produced by the opening of voltage-dependent channels.
options.opb: Increase its frequency if the intensity of the stimulus increases.
options.opc: It occurs after the binding of the neurotransmitter to the postsynaptic receptor.
options.opd: They occur if the trigger threshold is exceeded.
options.ope: It can be exciter or inhibitor.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Opening of voltage-dependent channels" -> "Influx of ions" -> "Generation of action potential" -> "Propagation of action potential along the neuron" -> "Release of neurotransmitters at the presynaptic terminal" -> "Binding of neurotransmitter to postsynaptic receptor" -> "Generation of postsynaptic potential" -> "Excitatory or inhibitory response" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Intensity of stimulus increases" -> "Greater depolarization of the neuron" -> "Higher likelihood of reaching the trigger threshold" -> "Generation of action potential" -> "Release of neurotransmitters at the presynaptic terminal" -> "Binding of neurotransmitter to postsynaptic receptor" -> "Excitatory or inhibitory response" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Exceeding trigger threshold" -> "Generation of action potential" -> "Propagation of action potential along the neuron" -> "Release of neurotransmitters at the presynaptic terminal" -> "Binding of neurotransmitter to postsynaptic receptor" -> "Excitatory or inhibitory response" -> 85%
analysis: A potential receiver refers to a postsynaptic neuron that receives signals from a presynaptic neuron. It can be excitatory or inhibitory depending on the neurotransmitter released. The potential receiver will generate an action potential if the stimulus exceeds the threshold, leading to the opening of voltage-dependent channels. The frequency of action potentials can increase with the intensity of the stimulus.
